lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Launch and planning: comparing housing options on total cost and fit

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic comparing housing options on total cost and fit task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Three fictional housing options are provided for a person about to live independently for the first time.
safetyNotes: All three housing options and their costs are fictional and provided for this lesson; the learner does not need to research or disclose any real housing situation to complete it.
materials: learner-local: the three provided fictional housing options

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l01-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l01-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l01-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l01-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Did your final recommendation match the priority you named in the warm-up? If not, what changed your mind?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u04-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Total-cost calculation accuracy: All three totals correctly include every recurring cost listed for that option. | Fit reasoning: Recommendation references at least two specific numbers or features from the comparison. | Reflective consistency: Reflection states clearly whether it matched and gives a reason. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Add a fourth fictional option with a cost the other three don't have (for example, a mandatory parking fee or a utility cap that triggers an extra charge above a certain usage) and have the learner redo the comparison with all four options.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic comparing housing options on total cost and fit task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: the three provided fictional housing options
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: comparing housing options on total cost and fit worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Three fictional housing options are provided for a person about to live independently for the first time.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact comparing housing options on total cost and fit decision or action.
Model move 2: Before looking at the numbers, name what would matter most to you.
Model move 3: For each of the three options, add up every recurring monthly cost listed (not just the rent number) to find its true total monthly cost.

Model check: Total-cost calculation accuracy: All three totals correctly include every recurring cost listed for that option. | Fit reasoning: Recommendation references at least two specific numbers or features from the comparison. | Reflective consistency: Reflection states clearly whether it matched and gives a reason.

resources.title: comparing housing options on total cost and fit action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for comparing housing options on total cost and fit.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: comparing housing options on total cost and fit coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Three fictional housing options are provided for a person about to live independently for the first time.
Coach direction: Before looking at the numbers, name what would matter most to you.
Learner prompt: Before looking at the numbers, what single feature of a living situation (cost, privacy, location, or who you live with) would matter most to you right now, and why?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: comparing housing options on total cost and fit complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: For each of the three options, add up every recurring monthly cost listed (not just the rent number) to find its true total monthly cost.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I calculated Riverside Studio's total monthly cost, including electricity and internet.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I calculated Maple House Share's total monthly cost, including the shared utilities amount.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I calculated Campus Suites' total monthly cost.
Response 4 (t2-p4): Write all three total monthly costs and show how you got each number.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: comparing housing options on total cost and fit minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Did your final recommendation match the priority you named in the warm-up? If not, what changed your mind?

Success checks: Total-cost calculation accuracy: All three totals correctly include every recurring cost listed for that option. | Fit reasoning: Recommendation references at least two specific numbers or features from the comparison. | Reflective consistency: Reflection states clearly whether it matched and gives a reason.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: comparing housing options on total cost and fit supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l01-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g11-u04-l01-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional comparing housing options on total cost and fit condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Total-cost calculation accuracy: All three totals correctly include every recurring cost listed for that option. | Fit reasoning: Recommendation references at least two specific numbers or features from the comparison. | Reflective consistency: Reflection states clearly whether it matched and gives a reason..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u04-l01-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
